newsitem.title: UK: British sales to foreign predators up in '96 - KPMG.
newsitem.headline: British sales to foreign predators up in '96 - KPMG.

text.p: British mergers and acquisitions involving foreign buyers rose eight percent to reach a record $38.5 billion in 1996, making Britain the main destination in Europe for overseas acquirers, a study said on Monday.

A KPMG Corporate Finance survey said foreign takeovers of British firms in 1996 exceeded the total for all other European Union countries combined and topped Britain's previous record of $36.3 billion, set in 1995.
Globally, the total value of cross-border mergers and acquisitions hit a record $263 billion last year, up from $237 billion, the study said.
Worldwide, only the United States beat Britain as a target for foreign predators in 1996.
U.S. companies attracted a record $68.03 billion of mergers and acquisitions from abroad last year, up from $61.42 billion in 1995, the survey said.
The buying spree in Britain last year was led by U.S. firms, spurred by the race to acquire Britain's regional electricity companies, the survey said.
U.S. firms spent nearly $20 billion on British takeovers last year, up from $13 billion in 1995.
Meanwhile, the value of acquisitions abroad by British firms rose to $34.1 billion, up from $27.0 billion in 1995.
U.S. companies remained the top target for British firms buying abroad, with U.S. sales to British companies rising 25 percent to $15.5 billion, the survey said.
